Performance

Source: vignettes/performance.Rmd
performance.Rmd

How the search stays fast

Every criterion in the package depends on the data only through a few quantities of the least-squares fit on the selected columns XSX_S: Y⊤HY=b⊤Mb,RSS=Y⊤Y−Y⊤HY,b=XS⊤Y,M=(XS⊤XS)−1. Y^\top H Y = b^\top M b, \qquad \mathrm{RSS} = Y^\top Y - Y^\top H Y, \qquad b = X_S^\top Y, \quad M = (X_S^\top X_S)^{-1}. So the n×nn \times n hat matrix HH is never formed. The search keeps MM and bb for the current model and scores each proposed move with a rank-one update.

  • Adding a column xzx_z: with u=XS⊤xzu = X_S^\top x_z, s=xz⊤xz−u⊤Mus = x_z^\top x_z - u^\top M u and e=xz⊤Y−b⊤Mue = x_z^\top Y - b^\top M u, Y⊤HY→Y⊤HY+ee⊤/s.Y^\top H Y \;\to\; Y^\top H Y + e\,e^\top / s .
  • Removing column jj: with β̂j=(Mb)j\hat\beta_j = (M b)_j, Y⊤HY→Y⊤HY−β̂j⊤β̂j/Mjj.Y^\top H Y \;\to\; Y^\top H Y - \hat\beta_j^\top \hat\beta_j / M_{jj} .

Scoring a move costs O(nK+K2)O(nK + K^2) for a model with KK variables, and MM is only updated when a move is accepted. Version 0.1.2 rebuilt HH for every proposal, at O(n2K)O(n^2 K) cost per move.

Timings

Speed-up over version 0.1.2 (Julia search only, EBIC or SIC, Apple M-series laptop). Both versions select the same variables at every step:

nn pp Passes 0.1.2 Current Speed-up
1000 100 2 0.18 s 0.002 s 91×
3000 100 2 1.29 s 0.005 s 247×
3000 100 2 (EBIC) 1.61 s 0.004 s 371×
2000 400 1 1.74 s 0.046 s 38×

Larger problems, timed from R with GICSelection() (EBIC, 10 true predictors, start from 20 variables, k = 100, Nsim = 3). The time includes copying X from R to Julia, and every run recovered exactly the 10 true predictors:

nn pp Time
500 1,000 0.9 s
1,000 5,000 7.6 s
2,000 10,000 26 s

To time your own problem:

library(GICHighDimension)
setup_julia()

set.seed(1)
n <- 1000; p <- 5000
X <- matrix(rnorm(n * p), n, p)
Y <- as.numeric(X[, 1:10] %*% rep(1, 10) + rnorm(n))

system.time(
  fit <- GICSelection(X, Y, 1:20, "Calculate_EBIC", "Calculate_EBIC_short",
                      k = 100, Nsim = 3)
)

The first call in a session also compiles the Julia code, which adds a few seconds once.
